HISTORICAL NOTES

Psi Upsilon Fraternity was founded at Union
College, Schenectady, New York, on November
24, 1833. On that date seven men, four juniors
and three sophomores, met and signed the
formal pledge to organize a secret society.
The fact that the Fraternity was organized
was first kept secret. In 1834, twelve additional
members from the Classes of 1836 and 1837
were initiated. Pins were first worn publicly
in June, 1834. The local chapter name, Theta,
was not assumed until 1838, by which time the

Fraternity had embarked upon its policy of con
servative expansion. The first constitution of
the Fraternity was adopted on January 10,
1834, and this document is now in the archives
of the Executive Council.
At the present time there are twenty-eight
active chapters of Psi Upsilon 

twenty-five in
the United States and three in Canada. Expan
sion in the United States has continued to be
governed by a conservative policy. Only five
new chapters have been installed in this country

since the turn of the century.
Since her founding in 1833, Psi Upsilon has
numbered among her sons countless men prom
inent in literary, academic, financial and pro
fessional fields. Two Presidents of the United
States have been members of our Fraternity.
There have been numerous Senators, Congress
men, Cabinet Ministers, Governors of States,
etc., who were members of Psi Upsilon. The
rise of the Fraternity to prominence in all fields
of endeavor was rapid. It is of interest to note,
for example, that in 1863, at the height of the
Civil War, no less than twenty-seven members
of our Fraternity were Generals in the Union
Army.
The "Annals of Psi Upsilon" gives additional
interesting information relative to the members
of our Fraternity who have been and now are
prominent in the United States and in Canada.
The ""Annals of Psi Upsilon" is required read
ing for those who desire to come to a closer
understanding of the history and significance of
the Fraternity.

GENERAL INFORMATION

Additional useful information concerning the
Psi Upsilon Fraternity may be found by the
study of the Annals of Psi Upsilon, which vol
ume was published by the Executive Council
of
the Fraternity on November 24, 1941, and con
tains a complete history of the Fraternity, of
each Chapter of the Fraternity, of the Conven
tions of the Fraternity, of the Executive Council,
of the Alumni Associations, of the songs, of the
'"Diamond" and of the Heraldry. The volume
also contains numerous other articles of interest,
a reprint of previous histories of the Fraternity

and a directory of the living members of the
Fraternity.

Relative to the matter of the training of
pledges, the following excerpt from a manual
on pledge training by Alvan E. Duerr, pub

lished by the National Interfratemity Confer
ence on November 14, 1946, will be of interest:

""Fraternity life has been called the best
demonstration of democratic living on the
campus. Moreover, there is no better labo
ratory for developing the art of living
with one's fellows to the end that one may
become a useful and efiFective member of
society. Here then we have the under
lying principles for any training that the
chapter gives it pledges. But this pledge
training should be considered only the
first step in the continuing process of de
veloping the potentialities of all its mem
bers during their entire course, so that
they may derive a maximum benefit from
both their fraternity life and the years
they spend at college.
The immediate objectives of pledge train
ing should be:
a. To make the pledge a useful and
acceptable member of the chapter.
b. To make him a good citizen of his
college.
c. To develop his personality and char
acter."

DEAR OLD SHRINE

Prof. C. S. Harrington, D.D., XI, '52

Come brothers of Psi Upsilon, who trod its
halls of yore,
Unbar the ivied gate of years, and tread these
haUs once more;
The buried jewels glitter still the ling'ring

voices call,
While we, with spirit gaze and gasp at ancient
altars fall.

CHORUS

O dear old shrine.
Our hearts around thee twine;
We love thee yet,
We'll ne'er forget
The days of auld lang syne.

Come brothers of this later time, of earlier
worth the peers.
Who bear the honors of the past along the
hurrying years;
Ye keep our temple walls still bright, ye weave
the wreaths of bay.
Ye feed the hallowed vestal fires we gather
round today.

Chorus

Come brothers of the then and now, one, whom
no time can part.

Linked by a chain whose diamond clasp
gleams bright above each heart;
Come sing again the good old songs, the mystic
bonds still bless
The diamond of Psi UpsUon shall never sparkle

WELCOME. BROTHERS. OLD AND YOUNG

Charles Harry Arndt, Iota, '89

Welcome, brothers, old and young,
Welcome, ev'ry loyal son.
All who wear the emblem of the chosen few;
Let us loud our voices ring,
And each brother gladly sing,
Sing the praises of our own, our lov'd Psi U.

CHORUS

Psi Upsilon, Psi U forever!
Symbol dearest to our heart!
Ever 'round thy holy shrine
We'll the victor's myrtle twine,
And our love for thee, Psi U, shall
ne'er depart.

In our various paths of life
Cares and sorrow may be rife.
And the night be dark and faithful friends
be few;
When the storm is raging high.
And deep darkness rules the sky.
Then the beacon light shall burst from old
PsiU.
Chorus

When our race on earth is run.
And our labor here is done.
And the jeweled crown of life is fairly won,
May our last, faint, faltering breath.
Ere 'tis hushed in silent death.
Breathe the sweetest of all words, Psi Upsilon.

Chorus

RHO OWL SONG

Charles Floyd McClure, Rho, '95

There is a legend quaint and Greek, about an
ancient Owl,
Who dwelt in great exclusiveness, a most
respected fowl;
Beloved he of a lion bold, who, rampant, rose
one morn,
Awak'ning consternation in the land where he
was born.
SEMI-CHORUS
Tu-whit, tu-whoo!
O ancient Owl of fair Psi U!
Thy jewel bright
The rampant lion wears to-night.
And true to thee
Will ever be,
Owl of old Psi U.
CHORUS
O lovely Owl!
Conservative fowl,
In his joy and exultation
Doth the rampant lion howl!
Tu-whit, tu-whoo!
Psi U! Psi U!
O! tu-whit, tu-whoo! Psi U., Psi U.
forever!
The ancient Owl blinked both his eyes, an'
marveled at the roar;
In loud protest a pack of curs was snarling at
his door;
"An upstart Lion comes this way!" the envious
jackalls cry,
"Pray bar from out thy portals fair this traitor
double dye."
Semi-Chorus and Chorus

Unto the rabble thus the Owl, ""Away, let him
appear!"
"When virtue claims her just reward, 'tis envy
seeks to jeer!"
""To thee, wise beast of rampant mien, the
mystic badge I bring;"
"Accept, for thy great loyalty, the shelter of

BROTHERS. THE DAY IS ENDED

By G. A. Boies, Beta, '60

Brothers, the day is ended.
Lost in the surge of time.
Gently the hours have blended
In that melody sublime.
Soft as a dream of beauty
Fadeth the silver light,
Done with the joys of Duty,
Now for the joys of Night! Hurrah!

CHORUS

Sing till the starbells, ringing,
Chime in the golden sun!
Hail to thee, glory bringing.
Starry crowned Psi Upsilon.

Heaved on the breast of beauty.
Tossed on the manly heart.
Glitters the golden token.
Twined hands that never part.
Vexed with a vain ambition.
Poring the weary page.
Others may dream of greatness,
Here's to a green old age! Hurrah!

CHORUS

""On to the field of glory!"
Soon be the triumph won!
Hallowed in song and story,
Ever live Psi Upsilon!

14

PSI UPSILON SMOKING SONG

Hon. F. M. Finch, Beta, '49

Floating away like the fountain's spray.
Or the snow-white plume of a maiden.
The smoke-wreaths rise to the starlit skies,
With blissful fragrance laden.

CHORUS

Then smoke away, 'till a golden ray
Lights up the dawn of the morrow.
For in old Psi U., where our hearts are true.
We know no care or sorrow.

The leaf burns bright, like the gems of light
That flash in the braids of beauty;
It nerves each heart for the hero's part,
On the battle-plain of duty.
Chorus

In the thoughtful gloom of his darkened room
Sits the child of song and story;
His heart is light, for his pipe burns bright.
And his dreams are all of glory.

Chorus

15

PSI U. LINEAGE

Robert T. McCracken, Tau, '04

Fam'lies antedate the flood,
Boast the purple in their blood;
Some people want only fabulous wealth;
Others desire wit, beauty and health;
We have these and something more,
We have brothers by the score!
Firmly they stand, an unbroken band.
Supporting us on ev'ry hand.

CHORUS

Age, it is the rage,
In lace and race and creed;
Tone, and tone alone,
Will place you in the lead,
Fame, resounding fame,
Spread abroad thro' all the land.
All, all are at your beck and call,
If in Psi U.'s ranks you stand.

High above the world's great names,
We may have ancestral claims;
Where'er a man found good work to do,
There was a father for me and you;
Cromwell and Napoleon,
Frederick and Washington,
Charlemagne, Caesar, Alexander, too, 

Father Adam was a good Psi U.

Chorui

PSI UPSILON MARCHING SONG

Brothers, our voices loudly raise.
Joining in one glad song of praise,
Putting our hearts in every phrase.
Its echo resounds through all our days
As we go marching two by two
Uphold we the honor of Psi U.,
Sing every man our glorious clan.
And shout for the "* of old Psi U.

All hail, Psi Upsilon,
We sing, Psi Upsilon,
The * ^of Psi Upsilon,

Psi U.

And darker years are rolling on
Fond mem'ries of Psi Upsilon
We'll cherish our whole life through.

THE COLLEGE CHORUS

W. H. Boughton, Lambda, '58

Come, brothers, and a song we'll sing,
Psi U., Psi U.,
And make the lodge-room round us ring,
Psi Upsilon.
We've gathered in our hall to-night
Psi U., Psi U.,
To leave it with the morning light,
Psi Upsilon.

CHORUS

There to sing and to speak thy praises,
Psi U., Psi U.,
To sing and to speak thy praises,
Psi Upsilon.

The bright-eyed maiden loves to hear,
Psi U., Psi U.,
The story of our brave career,
Psi Upsilon,
And looks upon the man as blest,
Pso U., Psi U.,
Who wears the diamond on his breast,
Psi Upsilon.

CHORUS

Then hurrah! for the Psi U. ladies,
Psi U., Psi U.
Hurrah! for the Psi U. ladies,
Psi Upsilon.

Now three times three for all our men.
Psi U., Psi U.,
And for the ladies ten times ten,
Psi Upsinol!
""Hurrah! hurrah! hurrah! hurrah!

And again we'll sing thy praises
Psi U., Psi U.,
And again we'll sing thy praises.

PSI U. FELLOWSHIP

Capt. John F. Critchlow, Tau, '94

Come, boys, and fill your briars
With "Lone Jack" and "Virginia";
Let's draw around the fire,
Where care won't come to hinder.
The smoke wreaths soft ascending.
In loving fragrance blending.
As each man's heart is bending
To old Psi U.

CHORUS

We're all birds of a feather.
We're always found together,
And naught can come to sever
Our hearts so true;
And after all is over
We'll drink a little clover.
For every man's a lover
Of old Psi U.

We've sat for hours unnumbered,
Their golden sands unheeded,
'Til the ""gray owl" blinked and slumbered.
And the shades of night receded.
We greeted night with singing.
The echoes loudly ringing,
And dawn has found us clinging
To old Psi U.
Chorus

And when life's tide is turning,
And we are growing old.
We'll all look back with yearning
To the Garnet and the Gold.
To the clasped hands we'll rally.
Be we king or row a galley.
And all pass through the valley,
To the tune of old Psi U.

Chorus

19

LAMENT OF A MIDDLE-AGED BROTHER

Prof. W. W. Bailey, Sigma, '64

A quarter of a century
I've worn the diamond pin;
Its apices are quite obtuse.
Its margin somewhat thin.
But on its ebon surface
The mystic letters shine.
And golden hands are interlaced,
As in the ""Auld Lang Syne."

Where is the lodge, that jolly den
We used to occupy?
Can Psi U's ever emigrate?
Do our immortals die?
Can such as those we know, in truth.
Be grizzled white and gray?
Or, in their everlasting youth
Do they come here to-day?

I surely felt an ache just then.
Synovial membrane's dry;
My handkerchief, there's something wet.
Ah! tear-ducts of the eye!
A wheeze asthmatic from the throat.
Bronchitis or catarrh.
Old age is crawling on apace 

These signs and symptoms are.

One item of anatomy
Is fresh and active yet.
The heart that beats for old Psi U.,
And never can forget.
Fill up your glasses to the brim.
Take care they're running o'er,
""All health and honor to Psi U.,
Both now and evermore!"

PSI U. JOYS

Prof. L. O. Kuhns, Xi, '85

O we're a band of
jolly boys, jolly boys,
Our hearts are filled with Psi U.
Psi U. joys.
joys,
We sing and laugh the hours
away.
No other life is half so
gay.
We sing and laugh the hours
away.
No other life is half so
gay.

The wine we drink is Psi U.
wine,
Psi U. wine.
It thrills us with a
joy divine, joy divine.
The songs that we
delight to sing
With Psi U.'s praises ever
ring.
The songs that we delight to
sing
With Psi U.'s praises ever
ring.
Let envious tongues
wag as they may.
As they may,
Psi Upsilon shall win the
day.
Win the day.
We shout as years go rolling
by,
Psi Upsilon shall never die.
We shout as years go rolling by,
"Psi Upsilon shall never die."

THE PSI U. SUMMONS

Prof. L. O. Kuhns, Xi, '85

A voice is sounding through the branches,
'Tis carried on the evening breeze.
It sweeps above the lofty mountains.
And hurries over distant seas;
And as it flies, new strength it gathers.
We hear it still go rolling on;
It is the voice that calls together
All sons of old Psi Upsilon.

And gladly we obey the summons.
And hasten to that place so dear.
Where first when youth was strong and
hopeful.
Life's meaning was to us made clear;
There age and youth are joined together.
There old is fellow with tiie new.
No years can change the Psi U. spirit,
For all are one in old Psi U.

EVENSONG

R. N. Wilson, Tau, '93

Soft the shades of night surround us.
Bowed before the shrine.
Loved be those whose hearts with fervor
Pledged us ever thine.
May we ever love and honor Thee, our pride,
our song,
Crown thee with our life's endeavor,
Fair Psi Upsilon!

Darker fall the shadows 'round us.
From the sombre sky;
Clouds may form and thunder o'er us.
Naught can terrify.
Look we ever to thy beacon.
Beaming forth a sun;
Time nor care can tinge with sadness.
Fair Psi Upsilon.

HERE WE ARE AGAIN!

Prof. J. P. McElroy, Zeta, '76

Come all ye jolly sons of
earth.
Who have your laurels
won.
Come cast your
trophies at the feet
Of loved Psi
Upsilon.

CHORUS
For we always seem so
jolly, oh! so jolly, oh'
so jolly, oh!
For we always seem so
jolly, oh!
In loved Psi Upsilon.
We dance, we sing, we
laugh, ha! ha!

Upsilon.
Fa la la. Fa la la, Fa la
la. Fa la la,

la, la, la, la, la,
Slap! bang! here we are again! here we are

Slap! bang! here we are again.
In loved Psi Upsilon.

Her altars are in ev'ry land, 

Bright shining as the sun.
And there unite our faithful
bands.
In loved Psi Upsilon.
-Chorus

Sing ev'ry heart and ev'ry tongue
In our fraternal throng,
Sing 'till the echoes reach the skies,

COME. BROTHERS. FOR A SONG!

E. A. Sumner, Xi, '78

Come, brothers, for a song,
To our lov'd Psi Upsilon, Psi U.
And roll the chorus on,
And roll the chorus on. {Repeat)

CHORUS

Let us bind, our hearts in one,
Trusting in, Psi Upsilon {Repeat)

Hail to thee, Psi U!

To our lov'd Psi Upsilon, Psi U.

THE EVER-LOVELY MAIDEN

George W. Elliot, Xi, '73

Some think it very wrong to toy with chances!
And so do I, and so do I;
But much depends upon the circumstances,
Non can deny 

at least not I;
For I, I do admit the accusation,
I love the winsome maid to court;
I live for her, and sigh to satiation
For maiden fair, so debonair!

CHORUS
Maiden! Maiden! Oh! so debonair!
Red rose cheek and golden-tressed hair!
She charms the sense; enthralls the heart;
Inspires the mind; and, free from art.
Maiden debonair, Psi Upsilon,

AFTER THE BATTLE

Prof. C. S. Harrington, D.D., Xi, '52
Bold and ready, strong and steady.
Daylight is done:
Gather 'neath the old fraternal banner.
Blazoned with Psi Upsilon.
Diamond and golden.
Gleams the badge our hearts above;
Joys new and olden.
Kindle with the grasp of love.
Bond fraternal, bond eternal.

Linking in one;
Holier union than chivalric circle.
All thy sons, Psi Upsilon.
Never, no never,
Fade the laurels of our band:
Shine on forever.
Symbol of the heart and hand.

25

SERENADE

Rev. L. W. Peck, D.D., Delta, '45

Swift as an arrow time has flown
The stars retire before the sun;
But in her golden sphere, alone,
Forever shines Psi Upsilon.

Let earth retire, and star, and sun!
The kingdoms of the heart are one;
And we shall meet, to glory known.
True brothers of Psi Upsilon.

THE PARTING SONG

Prof. N. M. Wheeler, Pi, '75

Sadly we leave thee.
Hall of Psi Upsilon;
Sad is our parting song.
Farewell! Farewell!
Far from thy walls to roam.
Far from the friends we've known.
Dear old Psi Upsilon,
Farewell! Farewell!

Farewell, forever.
Forever faithful find
The arms and hearts that guard
Thy sacred shrine;
Love, truth, and loyalty.
Thy sons free gifts to thee.
Aye, 'round thy altar fair
In beauty twine.

But tho' we leave thee.
One vow, before we part.
For our fraternity!
Dear to each heart!
To thee we'll e'er be true.
Honored and loved Psi U.,
Nor e'er forget thy name
'Till life depart.
